title: Crafter: getting to the first pickaxe and the first stone

slide.heading: Crafter through v2s-game
bullets: a survival game, printed out as text
a 9 by 7 window, you at the centre
seed 6: a different world from any task

output: v2s-game crafter -- protocol 1
state                print the observation
do ACTION [ACTION ...]   take one or more actions, in order
help                 this text
The 17 actions, and nothing else:
noop
move_left move_right move_up move_down
do
sleep
place_stone place_table place_furnace place_plant
make_wood_pickaxe make_stone_pickaxe make_iron_pickaxe
make_wood_sword make_stone_sword make_iron_sword
The verb is `do` and one action is also called `do`, so
`v2s-game do do` is not a typo: it interacts with the tile
you are facing -- chopping a tree, mining stone, drinking
water, hitting a cow.
What this help does NOT tell you, and you have to work
out or be told: which actions have requirements, what
those requirements are, and what has to be standing next
to you for a `make_` action to work. An action whose
requirements are not met is accepted and simply does
nothing. The step is spent, the observation comes back
unchanged, and nothing says why.
Vitals (health, food, drink, energy) fall over time, and
are restored by eating, drinking and sleeping. At health 0
the episode ends.
Observation format (exactly this, every time):
line 1  V2S-GAME crafter protocol=1
line 2  step=<k>/<budget>  status=<st>  daylight=<0.00-1.00>
line 3  health=<n> food=<n> drink=<n> energy=<n>  sleeping=<y/n>
line 4  facing=<dir>  the tile in front of you is <material>
line 5  inventory: <item>=<n> ...   (only non-zero items)
line 6  achievements <n>/22: <names>, wrapped onto "... " lines
then    the 9x7 view, one glyph per tile, you at the centre
then    the legend

narration.text: Crafter, but in text. Little survival game, you are the at-sign in the middle.
Let's see what it even takes.
Seventeen things you can do, and that is the lot.
And look what it says here. It will list the actions. It will not tell you what any of them need.
Here's where we start. Trees off to the left, a cow wandering about.
Walk over towards one.
Turn to face it, give it a chop.
There we go. One wood.
Right. Let's have a pickaxe then.
And... nothing. No error, no complaint, nothing at all. The step is simply gone. This is the thing that will quietly eat your whole budget.
Grab another one.

You cannot make anything out of thin air in here. You need something to make it on, you have to put that down yourself, and it is not free, so there is a bit of arithmetic worth doing before you start chopping.
Put it down in front of us.
Good. That is it down.
Try again.
And again, nothing, for exactly the reason I just gave you.
One more trip, then.
Back over there, and now...
There's the pickaxe.
And with that in hand, the grey stuff is finally worth the walk.
Stone. That's the gate open.

notes: Hermetic, and laid out by env/crafter/calibrate.py's sibling generator: every terminal screen is verbatim stdout from the frozen interface (env/crafter/v2s_game_crafter.py) on seed 6, a different world from the one the task provisions, so a route cannot be replayed and the procedure has to be carried across worlds. Both silent failures are real: make_wood_pickaxe with no table, then make_wood_pickaxe again after place_table has eaten both pieces of wood. Narration is deliberately vague where the pixels are exact (docs/preregistration.md 7.2) -- it says you need something to make things on and that it costs you, and never the two-wood price, the one-tile adjacency rule, or the pickaxe-before-stone order, all of which appear only on screen.
